actions.action: Rinse plants under sink or shower spray, especially leaf undersides
Spray with insecticidal soap, neem oil, or dish soap solution, repeating every 5-7 days for 3-4 weeks
Test spray on one leaf and check for burn after a day
Prune badly damaged or curled leaves and discard them
Check soil surface and nearby plants for stragglers
Use yellow sticky traps if flying insects are seen
Check whether bugs fly up and sit on leaf undersides to tell whitefly from aphids
Rinse herbs well before eating and wait the label interval after treatment
Inspect new plants before placing near others
Send a closer photo if treatments fail

reason: The answer names aphids as the main cause and puts rinsing under the sink plus pruning damaged leaves near the top, which matches the fix that worked; whitefly is only a side note, and the soap or neem step is reasonable and protected by a leaf test.
